alert_news.title: India's First Indigenous Bullet Train Takes Shape At BEML's Bengaluru Facility
bullets: India’s first indigenously manufactured bullet train is being developed at BEML Bengaluru for the Mumbai–Ahmedabad High‑Speed Rail corridor.
The eight‑coach trainset will be 202 m long, carry 557 passengers, and run at an operational speed of 249 kmph (test speed 280 kmph).

alert_news.title: 45 Mins To 15 Mins! India's 1st Public Ropeway Project In Varanasi To Cut Travel Time On ...
bullets: India’s first public transport ropeway will connect Varanasi Cantt Railway Station to Godowlia Chowk over a 4.2 km stretch.
The project will deploy 220 cable cars, cost ₹675 crore, and is expected to reduce travel time from 45 minutes to 15–16 minutes.

alert_news.title: Bihar Became India's First State with Silt Management Policy 2026
bullets: Bihar is the first Indian state to introduce a comprehensive silt management policy, named Bihar Water Source Restoration and Silt Management Policy 2026.
Policy, in partnership with NHAI under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, aims to manage river silt, improve flood control, and repurpose silt as filling material for national highways.

alert_news.title: Gold itna paas tha kaise jaane deti, says India's first woman wrestling world champion
bullets: Manisha Bhanwala became India's first woman wrestling world champion, winning gold in the 59kg freestyle category at the World Championships in Astana, Kazakhstan.
Her victory marks the first Indian woman to secure a world title in wrestling, a historic milestone for Indian sports.

alert_news.title: India's First Wushu Medal at Youth Olympics Won by Rajkumari
bullets: Rajkumari Lanchenbi Chanu earned India's first wushu medal at the Youth Olympic Games 2026, winning bronze in women's changquan combined.
First time wushu was a medal sport at the Youth Olympics.
Event held in Dakar, Senegal, marking India's third medal at the Games.

alert_news.title: India's First Hydrogen-Powered Train Operates on Jind‑Sonipat Section
bullets: India’s first indigenous hydrogen‑powered train, inaugurated 17 July 2026, runs on the Jind‑Sonipat section of Northern Railway.
Developed by Indian Railways and RDSO, it uses a Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell and is supported by a dedicated hydrogen storage and refuelling facility at Jind, Haryana.
